did: T3 - the hostile/civilian discriminator is a field on the Entity, not the component walk.
evidence: entity+0x9C = packed u32: bits0-2 kind, bits3-8 role, bits9-14 variant, bits15+ flags. Proof: sub_4EDCF0 @0x4edcf0..0x4edd1f does *this = *this & 0xFFFF8007 | (8 * (a3 & 0x3F | ((a4 & 0x3F) << 6))); sub_6B5810 @0x6b5813..0x6b582d = SetKind, mask 0xFC078000. Role name table sub_1406C70 @0x1406c70: 1=Guard, 2=Civilian, 3=Thief, 5=Mercenary, 19=Animal, 23=Naval (naval role 23 confirmed read back at 0x199a1d9). Game's own predicates, __thiscall, this = &entity->field9C: sub_54EC00 @0x54ec00 = (v and 7)==2 and (v and 0x1F8)==0x10 = civilian (callers lea ecx,[e+9Ch] @0x199a66a and @0x1aedf88); sub_73B4B0 @0x73b4b0 = (v and 7)==3 and (v and 0x1F8)==8 = guard (caller @0x1619a0c); inline guard test then GetComponentByType @0x1403c82..0x1403cb1. GetComponentByType @0x5200e5 reads +0x60/+0x66, so it is the same Entity the walk uses.
predicate: unsigned a = *(unsigned*)((char*)e + 0x9C); kind = a and 7; role = (a >> 3) and 0x3F. IsSoldier = kind==3 and role==1. IsCivilian = kind==2 and role==2. One dword load, no component walk, immune to the +0x64/+0x66 bug.
